size.note: Newman's Birds gives 90 cm on the White-breasted Cormorant page.

habitat: Singly or in groups on coastal rocks, islands and estuaries, and on large inland waters.
summary: A common or localised resident. Large, with a white throat and breast. The upperwings and tail are dark brown and the wing feathers are edged black. The adult has green eyes, a pale grey bill with a darker culmen and yellow facial skin. The immature has entirely white underparts, much whiter than an immature Reed Cormorant. Newman’s page uses Phalacrocorax lucidus and the name White-breasted Cormorant. This file keeps Phalacrocorax carbo and Great (White-breasted) Cormorant. The Kemp paper name Whitebreasted Cormorant and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Reed Cormorant is considerably smaller. Its immature is off-white below, never as white as an immature White-breasted Cormorant.

research.note: Newman calls it a common or localised resident, so status is resident and all twelve months are listed. The immature upperparts are not described, which is why this needs review. The stored scientific name Phalacrocorax carbo was left unchanged. Population figures, the Kemp paper name Whitebreasted Cormorant and the code RB were left unchanged.
